# Jubilees Chapter 34 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** The Amorite war; Joseph sold; Isaac dies

---

**34:1** In the forty-fifth jubilee, third week, sixth year, Jacob and all his sons settled in the region east of Shechem.

**34:2** Seven Amorite kings came together, blades drawn, to wipe out Jacob and his family. It was a mistake. Jacob's sons overwhelmed them in the highlands of Shechem, killed them all, and seized everything they owned.

**34:3** Here's the count: Judah killed King Mahalath. Dan killed his opponent. Naphtali killed Hazor. Gad killed Phineas. Asher killed Boaz of Betoron. Zebulun killed his king. Reuben killed his king.

**34:4** Seven kings dead, seven kingdoms' worth of plunder. They brought it all back to Shechem.

**34:5** In the seventh year of that same week, Joseph was looking for his brothers. He went to Dothan first, didn't find them there, then tracked them east toward Shechem — and found them.

**34:6** The moment they saw him, the brothers began plotting. "Let's sell him to those Ishmaelite traders," Judah suggested. The rest agreed.

**34:7** A caravan of Midianite merchants came along. The brothers pulled Joseph out of the pit and sold him — twenty silver coins for their own brother. The traders took him to Egypt.

**34:8** To cover their tracks, they slaughtered a goat, soaked Joseph's coat in the blood, and sent it home to Jacob.

**34:9** Jacob was devastated. "My son has been killed by a wild animal." He tore his clothes, put on sackcloth, and grieved for days on end.

**34:10** During this period, Deborah — the old nurse who had served Rebekah — died. Jacob buried her under the oak tree near Bethel. He named the spot "Oak of Weeping."

**34:11** In the forty-fifth jubilee, fifth week, first year, Jacob sent Judah to visit their grandfather Isaac. The visit strengthened them both. Jacob was happy whenever he was near his father, and all of Jacob's sons adored Isaac.

**34:12** When Isaac fell ill, Esau and Jacob both came to his bedside. Seeing both his sons calmed him. "I'm ready," he said. "I've had a hundred and eighty years."

**34:13** Isaac died in the forty-fifth jubilee, sixth week, first year. Both his sons buried him.

**34:14** Esau took his family to Edom, to the Seir highlands, and settled there. Jacob stayed at Mamre near Hebron.

**34:15** All twelve of Jacob's sons married and had children of their own.

**34:16** Reuben had four sons: Enoch, Phallu, Hezron, Carmi. Simeon had five: Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar. Levi had three: Gershon, Kohath, Merari. Judah had five: Er, Onan, Shelah, Perez, Zerah.

**34:17** Two years later — in the sixth week, second year — famine hit every country except Egypt. Jacob sent most of his sons to Egypt to buy grain. He kept Benjamin home.

**34:18** By then Joseph was Egypt's second-in-command, managing Pharaoh's entire grain supply. He was thirty when he entered Pharaoh's service.

**34:19** When his brothers walked into Egypt, Joseph recognized them instantly. They had no idea who he was.

**34:20** "Bring your youngest brother to me," Joseph told them. He held Simeon hostage until they came back with Benjamin.

---

*PNEUMA notes: The Amorite war (vv.1-4) is unique to Jubilees/Testament of Judah tradition — it has no parallel in Genesis and gives Jacob's sons a martial heroic tradition. The compression of the Joseph story here is dramatic and effective.*
